user_groups.summary: Zabbix user groups that provisioned users of the matching group are added to.

usrgrpid.summary: ID of the user group that provisioned users are added to.

attribute.summary: The identity provider attribute that holds the send-to address.

mediatypeid.summary: The ID of the media type created for provisioned users.

name.summary: The name of the media mapping.

period.summary: When the media is active, as a time period specification; defaults to 1-7,00:00-24:00.

severity.summary: The problem severities that the media is used for, as a bitmask: 1 not classified, 2 information, 4 warning, 8 average, 16 high, 32 disaster. Defaults to 63, all severities.

userdirectory_mediaid.summary: The ID of an existing media mapping.

base_dn.summary: The LDAP base path under which user accounts are searched, for example ou=Users,dc=example,dc=org; for direct user binding it contains the %{user} placeholder.

bind_dn.summary: The distinguished name of the LDAP account used to bind and search the server; empty for anonymous binding and for direct user binding.

bind_password.summary: The password of the LDAP bind account; empty for anonymous binding and for direct user binding. It is never returned by the API.

group_basedn.summary: The LDAP base path under which groups are searched for the group membership check; ignored during provisioning when a group membership attribute is set.

group_filter.summary: The LDAP filter used to find the groups a user belongs to, with the %{attr}, %{groupattr}, %{host}, %{user} and %{ref} placeholders; defaults to (%{groupattr}=%{user}) and is ignored during provisioning when a group membership attribute is set.

group_member.summary: The LDAP group attribute that lists the members of a group, used for the group membership check; ignored during provisioning when a group membership attribute is set.

group_membership.summary: The LDAP user attribute that lists the groups the user belongs to, for example memberOf.

group_name.summary: The directory attribute that holds the group name used to map directory groups to Zabbix user groups, for example cn.

idp_type.summary: The directory type to test; only LDAP directories can be tested.

port.summary: The TCP port of the LDAP server.

provision_groups.summary: The group mappings to evaluate for the test user when provisioning is enabled; required in that case.

provision_media.summary: The media type mappings to evaluate for the test user when provisioning is enabled.

provision_status.summary: Whether users authenticated through this directory are provisioned automatically; provisioning also requires LDAP or SAML just-in-time provisioning to be enabled in the authentication settings. Disabled by default.

search_attribute.summary: The LDAP attribute matched against the login name to find the user account, for example uid or sAMAccountName.

search_filter.summary: A custom LDAP filter used to locate the user account at login, with the %{attr} and %{user} placeholders; the server uses (%{attr}=%{user}) when empty.

start_tls.summary: Whether the LDAP connection is upgraded to TLS with StartTLS; must be off for ldaps:// servers. Off by default.

test_password.summary: The password of the account whose login is tested against the LDAP server; required.

test_username.summary: The username of the account whose login is tested against the LDAP server; required.

user_lastname.summary: The directory attribute (also the SCIM attribute when SCIM provisioning is on) whose value becomes the surname of a provisioned user, for example sn.

user_ref_attr.summary: The LDAP user attribute whose value replaces the %{ref} placeholder in the group filter, for example cn or uid.

user_username.summary: The directory attribute (also the SCIM attribute when SCIM provisioning is on) whose value becomes the name of a provisioned user, for example givenName or displayName.

userdirectoryid.summary: The identifier of a stored LDAP directory whose saved settings, including the bind password, are used for any connection property the request leaves out.

host.summary: Host name or IP address of the LDAP server.

active.summary: Whether the media is enabled or disabled; the default is enabled.

attribute.summary: Name of the directory attribute that holds the send-to address for the media.

mediatypeid.summary: ID of the media type of the media that provisioned users receive.

name.summary: Name of the media mapping.

period.summary: When the media is active, as a time period such as "1-7,00:00-24:00", which is the default; user macros are allowed.

severity.summary: Event severities the media is used for, as a bitmask: 1 not classified, 2 information, 4 warning, 8 average, 16 high, 32 disaster. The default is 63, all severities.

base_dn.summary: The LDAP base path under which user accounts are searched, for example ou=Users,dc=example,dc=org; for direct user binding it contains the %{user} placeholder.

bind_dn.summary: The distinguished name of the LDAP account used to bind and search the server; empty for anonymous binding and for direct user binding.

bind_password.summary: The password of the LDAP bind account; empty for anonymous binding and for direct user binding. It is never returned by the API.

description.summary: A free-form description of the user directory; applies to LDAP directories.

encrypt_assertions.summary: Whether SAML assertions are encrypted. Off by default.

encrypt_nameid.summary: Whether the SAML name ID is encrypted. Off by default.

group_basedn.summary: The LDAP base path under which groups are searched for the group membership check; ignored during provisioning when a group membership attribute is set.

group_filter.summary: The LDAP filter used to find the groups a user belongs to, with the %{attr}, %{groupattr}, %{host}, %{user} and %{ref} placeholders; defaults to (%{groupattr}=%{user}) and is ignored during provisioning when a group membership attribute is set.

group_member.summary: The LDAP group attribute that lists the members of a group, used for the group membership check; ignored during provisioning when a group membership attribute is set.

group_membership.summary: The LDAP user attribute that lists the groups the user belongs to, for example memberOf.

group_name.summary: The directory attribute that holds the group name used to map directory groups to Zabbix user groups, for example cn.

idp_certificate.summary: The PEM content of the identity provider certificate; accepted only when SAML certificates are kept in the database, and never returned by the API.

idp_entityid.summary: The URI that identifies the SAML identity provider in SAML messages.

idp_type.summary: The authentication protocol of the identity provider behind the directory, LDAP or SAML; only one SAML directory can exist.

name.summary: Unique user directory name; an LDAP directory requires it, and the SAML directory leaves it empty unless an update sets it.

nameid_format.summary: The SAML name ID format requested from the identity provider, for example urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent.

port.summary: The TCP port of the LDAP server.

provision_groups.summary: The mappings from directory group name patterns to the Zabbix user role and user groups assigned to provisioned users; required when provisioning is enabled.

provision_media.summary: The mappings from directory attributes to user media for provisioned users; the given list replaces the existing mappings, and an entry that carries an existing mapping ID updates that mapping.

provision_status.summary: Whether users authenticated through this directory are provisioned automatically; provisioning also requires LDAP or SAML just-in-time provisioning to be enabled in the authentication settings. Disabled by default.

scim_status.summary: Whether SCIM provisioning is enabled for the SAML directory. Off by default.

search_attribute.summary: The LDAP attribute matched against the login name to find the user account, for example uid or sAMAccountName.

search_filter.summary: A custom LDAP filter used to locate the user account at login, with the %{attr} and %{user} placeholders; the server uses (%{attr}=%{user}) when empty.

sign_assertions.summary: Whether SAML assertions are signed. Off by default.

sign_authn_requests.summary: Whether SAML authentication requests are signed. Off by default.

sign_logout_requests.summary: Whether SAML logout requests are signed. Off by default.

sign_logout_responses.summary: Whether SAML logout responses are signed. Off by default.

sign_messages.summary: Whether SAML messages are signed. Off by default.

slo_url.summary: The URL of the identity provider's SAML single logout service, to which logout requests are sent.

sp_certificate.summary: The PEM content of the service provider certificate; accepted only when SAML certificates are kept in the database, and never returned by the API.

sp_entityid.summary: The identifier of Zabbix as the SAML service provider, a URL or any string.

sp_private_key.summary: The PEM content of the service provider private key; accepted only when SAML certificates are kept in the database, and never returned by the API.

sso_url.summary: Address that receives authentication requests: the identity provider's SAML single sign-on endpoint.

start_tls.summary: Whether the LDAP connection is upgraded to TLS with StartTLS; must be off for ldaps:// servers. Off by default.

user_lastname.summary: The directory attribute (also the SCIM attribute when SCIM provisioning is on) whose value becomes the surname of a provisioned user, for example sn.

user_ref_attr.summary: The LDAP user attribute whose value replaces the %{ref} placeholder in the group filter, for example cn or uid.

user_username.summary: The directory attribute (also the SCIM attribute when SCIM provisioning is on) whose value becomes the name of a provisioned user, for example givenName or displayName.

userdirectoryid.summary: The identifier of the user directory to update.

username_attribute.summary: The SAML attribute (also the SCIM attribute when SCIM provisioning is on) whose value is compared with the Zabbix username at login.

host.summary: Host name or IP address of the LDAP server.

debug_mode.summary: Whether debug mode is enabled for the group members: 0 disabled, 1 enabled.

gui_access.summary: Frontend authentication method of the group members: 0 system default, 1 internal, 2 LDAP, 3 frontend access disabled.

mfa_status.summary: Whether multi-factor authentication is required for the group members: 0 disabled, 1 enabled.

mfaid.summary: ID of the multi-factor authentication method used by the group members.

name.summary: Name of the user group.

proxy_group_mode.summary: How the proxy groups listed for the group are applied: 0 denies access to them, 1 allows access only to them.

proxy_mode.summary: How the proxies listed for the group are applied: 0 denies access to them, 1 allows access only to them.

userdirectoryid.summary: ID of the user directory used for LDAP authentication of the group members.

users_status.summary: Whether the group members are enabled: 0 enabled, 1 disabled.

usrgrpid.summary: ID of the user group.

id.summary: The ID of the host group that the permission applies to.

permission.summary: The access granted: 0 denied, 2 read-only, 3 read-write.

id.summary: ID of the host group the permission applies to.

permission.summary: Access the group's users have to the host group: denied, read-only or read-write.

proxy_groupid.summary: ID of a proxy group in the user group's proxy group list.

proxyid.summary: ID of a proxy in the user group's proxy list.

id.summary: The ID of the host or template group that the permission applies to.

permission.summary: The access granted: 0 denied, 2 read-only, 3 read-write.

id.summary: ID of the host group the permission applies to.

permission.summary: Access the group's users have to the host group: denied, read-only or read-write.

groupid.summary: ID of the host group the tag filter applies to.

tag.summary: Name of the problem tag that grants access; empty grants access to all problems of the host group.

usrgrpid.summary: ID of the user group the tag filter belongs to.

value.summary: Value of the problem tag; empty matches any value.

groupid.summary: ID of the host group the tag filter applies to.

tag.summary: Name of the problem tag the group's users can see; empty allows all problems in the host group.

value.summary: Value of the problem tag the group's users can see; empty allows any value.

id.summary: The ID of the template group that the permission applies to.

permission.summary: The access granted: 0 denied, 2 read-only, 3 read-write.

id.summary: ID of the template group the permission applies to.

permission.summary: Access the group's users have to the template group: denied, read-only or read-write.

debug_mode.summary: Whether debug mode is enabled in the frontend for members of the group.

gui_access.summary: How members of the group authenticate to the frontend: the system default method, internal authentication, LDAP, or no frontend access at all.

hostgroup_rights.summary: The permissions the group has on host groups; each entry pairs a host group ID with deny, read-only or read-write access.

mfa_status.summary: Whether multi-factor authentication is required for members of the group.

mfaid.summary: The ID of the multi-factor authentication method the group uses; 0 means the default method. Applies only when multi-factor authentication is enabled.

name.summary: The unique name of the user group.

proxies.summary: The proxies in the proxy access list of the group.

proxy_group_mode.summary: Whether the proxy group access list of the group is an allow list, granting access to only the listed proxy groups, or a deny list, granting access to every proxy group except them.

proxy_groups.summary: The proxy groups in the proxy group access list of the group.

proxy_mode.summary: Whether the proxy access list of the group is an allow list, granting access to only the listed proxies, or a deny list, granting access to every proxy except them; covers proxies that are not in a proxy group.

rights.summary: The permissions the group has on host groups. Deprecated in Zabbix 7.0 and removed in 7.4; use the host group rights instead.

tag_filters.summary: The tag-based permissions of the group; each entry limits access in a host group to problems whose tags match the given tag name and value.

templategroup_rights.summary: The permissions the group has on template groups; each entry pairs a template group ID with deny, read-only or read-write access.

userdirectoryid.summary: The ID of the user directory used to authenticate members of the group; applies when frontend access uses the system default method or LDAP.

users.summary: The users to place in the group, identified by user ID; the list replaces the current members.

users_status.summary: Whether the members of the group are enabled; when disabled, they cannot log in or use the API.

usrgrpid.summary: User group ID.

userids.summary: IDs of the users to place in the group; deprecated in 7.0 and removed in 7.4. Use <see cref="Users"/>.

userid.summary: ID of a user who is a member of the user group.

userData.summary: If set, return information about the authenticated user together with the session token instead of the token alone.

username.summary: Login name of the user. Required.

description.summary: Help text shown with the field.

label.summary: Label of the field; required for text, list, and checkbox fields.

options.summary: Choices of the field: value and text pairs for a list, or a single checked and unchecked value pair for a checkbox.

priority.summary: Position of the field in the wizard; fields are ordered by ascending value.

regex.summary: Regular expression the entered value must match; applies only to text fields.

required.summary: Whether a value must be entered; applies to text and list fields.

section_name.summary: Name of the wizard section the field is placed in.

type.summary: Kind of input field shown for the macro in the host wizard: none, text field, list, or checkbox.

checked.summary: Macro value set when the checkbox is selected; used by checkbox fields.

text.summary: Label shown for the list option; used by list fields and must not be empty.

unchecked.summary: Macro value set when the checkbox is cleared; used by checkbox fields.

value.summary: Macro value that the list option sets; used by list fields.

checked.summary: The macro value set when the checkbox is selected.

text.summary: The text shown for a list option.

unchecked.summary: The macro value set when the checkbox is cleared.

value.summary: The macro value that a list option sets.

description.summary: Help text shown with the field in the host wizard.

label.summary: Label of the field in the host wizard; required for text, list and checkbox fields.

options.summary: Choices offered by a list field, or the checked and unchecked values of a checkbox field.

priority.summary: Position of the field in the host wizard; fields are ordered by this value.

regex.summary: Regular expression that the value of a text field must match; empty for no check.

required.summary: Whether the user must fill in the field; applies to text and list fields.

section_name.summary: Name of the host wizard section that holds the field.

type.summary: Kind of host wizard field that presents the macro: none, text box, list or checkbox.

description.summary: A free-form description of the macro.

type.summary: How the macro value is stored and shown: as plain text (the default), as a masked secret, or as a reference to a vault secret.

value.summary: The value of the global macro; required. For a secret macro it is write-only, and for a vault secret it is the path to the secret in the vault.

description.summary: A free-form description of the macro.

globalmacroid.summary: The identifier of the global macro to update.

type.summary: How the macro value is stored and shown: as plain text (the default), as a masked secret, or as a reference to a vault secret.

value.summary: The value of the global macro; for a secret macro it is write-only, and for a vault secret it is the path to the secret in the vault.

automatic.summary: Whether the macro is managed by discovery; only the user-managed value is accepted, and a discovered macro must be converted this way before it can be changed.

config.summary: How the macro is presented as an input field in the host wizard.

description.summary: A free-form description of the macro.

hostmacroid.summary: The identifier of the host macro to update.

type.summary: How the macro value is stored and shown: as plain text (the default), as a masked secret, or as a reference to a vault secret.

value.summary: The value of the macro; for a secret macro it is write-only, and for a vault secret it is the path to the secret in the vault.

period.summary: Days and hours in which this media may deliver, written as a time period such as 1-7,00:00-24:00 (every day, all day), which is the default.

sendto.summary: Addresses, user names, or other recipient identifiers that notifications are sent to; email media types accept several addresses.

severity.summary: Problem severities that trigger notifications, as a bitmask: 1 not classified, 2 information, 4 warning, 8 average, 16 high, 32 disaster; the server uses 63, all severities, when omitted.

active.summary: Whether the media is enabled or disabled; the default is enabled.

mediaid.summary: ID of an existing media to update; omit it to add a new media.

period.summary: When the media is active, as a time period such as "1-7,00:00-24:00", which is the default; user macros are allowed.

sendto.summary: Addresses the notifications are sent to; email media accept several addresses, other media types one.

severity.summary: Event severities the media is used for, as a bitmask: 1 not classified, 2 information, 4 warning, 8 average, 16 high, 32 disaster. The default is 63, all severities.

autologin.summary: Whether the user stays logged in across browser sessions.

autologout.summary: Idle time after which the user session expires, in seconds or with a time suffix: 0 never expires, otherwise 90 seconds to 1 day. Defaults to 15m.

current_passwd.summary: Current password of the user. Required when users change their own password.

default_maintenance_period.summary: Default duration offered when this user creates a maintenance, from 5 minutes to 999 days 23 hours 59 minutes; rounded down to whole minutes. Defaults to 1h.

lang.summary: Locale the frontend uses for this user, such as en_US; default follows the system-wide setting.
lang.name: Language

medias.summary: Notification media of the user; replaces the current media.

name.summary: First name of the user.
name.name: FirstName

passwd.summary: New password of the user, checked against the password policy.

refresh.summary: Automatic page refresh period, in seconds or with a time suffix, up to 1 hour. Defaults to 30s.

roleid.summary: ID of the user role, which sets the user type and what the user may access.

rows_per_page.summary: Number of rows shown per page in frontend lists, from 1 to 999999. Defaults to 50.

theme.summary: Frontend theme of the user, or default for the system default.

timezone.summary: Time zone of the user, such as Europe/London, or default for the system default.

url.summary: Frontend page the user is sent to after logging in.

userid.summary: ID of the user to update. Required.

username.summary: Login name of the user; must be unique.

usrgrps.summary: User groups of the user; replaces the current memberships. Each entry needs only a user group ID.

usrgrpid.summary: The ID of a user group that the user belongs to.

newvalue.summary: The text shown in place of a matching value.

type.summary: How the value is matched: equals, greater than or equal, less than or equal, within a range, matches a regular expression, or default for unmatched values.

value.summary: The original value, range or pattern that the mapping matches; empty for the default mapping.

mappings.summary: The rules that translate item values into display text, applied in order.

name.summary: Value map name; no two maps on a host or template may share it.

uuid.summary: The universally unique identifier of the value map, used to match value maps when templates are imported; set only for value maps that belong to templates.

ApmLog.summary: An OpenTelemetry log record that Zabbix stores for application performance monitoring, as <c>apmlog.get</c> returns it.

timestamp.summary: Time the log record was observed, as text with nanoseconds (<c>YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.nnnnnnnnn</c>, UTC).

traceid.summary: ID of the trace the log record belongs to, as hexadecimal text; empty when the record is not part of a trace.

spanid.summary: ID of the span the log record belongs to, as hexadecimal text; empty when the record is not part of a span.

trace_flags.summary: W3C trace flags of the trace context the record was written in; bit 1 marks a sampled trace.

severity_text.summary: Severity of the record as its source names it, such as INFO or ERROR.

severity_number.summary: Severity of the record as an OpenTelemetry severity number, from 1 (TRACE) to 24 (FATAL4); 0 when unspecified.

service_name.summary: Name of the service that wrote the record (the <c>service.name</c> resource attribute).

body.summary: Body of the log record, the message itself.

resource_schema_url.summary: Schema URL of the resource attributes.

resource_attributes.summary: Attributes of the resource that wrote the record, by key.

scope_schema_url.summary: Schema URL of the instrumentation scope.

scope_name.summary: Name of the instrumentation scope that wrote the record.

scope_version.summary: Version of the instrumentation scope that wrote the record.

scope_attributes.summary: Attributes of the instrumentation scope, by key.

log_attributes.summary: Attributes of the log record itself, by key.

event_name.summary: Name of the event the record describes; empty when it describes none.

ApmLogGetParameters.summary: Query parameters for the <c>apmlog.get</c> API method.

time_from.summary: Return only log records at or after the given Unix time. Required.

time_till.name: TimeTo
time_till.summary: Return only log records before the given Unix time. Required.

filter.summary: Return only log records whose properties exactly match the given values; each key is a property name and each value is a single value or an array of accepted values.

search.summary: Return only log records whose given text properties contain the given strings; matching is case-insensitive.

searchByAny.summary: When true, return results that match any of the Filter or Search criteria instead of all of them.

startSearch.summary: When true, a Search value matches only at the start of a property instead of anywhere in it.

excludeSearch.summary: When true, return results that do not match the Search criteria.

searchWildcardsEnabled.summary: When true, an asterisk in a Search value matches any sequence of characters.

output.summary: Properties to return for each of the log records; when omitted, all properties are returned.

countOutput.summary: When true, return the number of matching records instead of the records themselves.

sortfield.summary: Properties to sort the results by; accepted values are timestamp, traceid, spanid, trace_flags, severity_text, severity_number, service_name, resource_schema_url, scope_schema_url, scope_name, scope_version and event_name.

sortorder.summary: Sort direction for each sort field, ASC (the default) or DESC.

limit.summary: Maximum number of records to return.

offset.summary: Number of matching records to skip before the first one returned.

traceids.summary: Return only log records of the given traces.

spanids.summary: Return only log records of the given spans.

with_flags_on.summary: Return only log records whose trace flags have every bit of the given mask set.

with_flags_off.summary: Return only log records whose trace flags have no bit of the given mask set.

severity_numbers.summary: Return only log records of the given OpenTelemetry severity numbers, from 1 to 24.

resource_attributes.summary: Return only log records whose resource attributes match the given conditions.

resource_attributes_evaltype.summary: How the resource attribute conditions combine: <c>AndOr</c> (the default) combines conditions on the same key with or and the rest with and; <c>Or</c> combines all of them with or.

scope_attributes.summary: Return only log records whose scope attributes match the given conditions.

scope_attributes_evaltype.summary: How the scope attribute conditions combine: <c>AndOr</c> (the default) combines conditions on the same key with or and the rest with and; <c>Or</c> combines all of them with or.

log_attributes.summary: Return only log records whose own attributes match the given conditions.

log_attributes_evaltype.summary: How the log attribute conditions combine: <c>AndOr</c> (the default) combines conditions on the same key with or and the rest with and; <c>Or</c> combines all of them with or.

ApmLogResourceAttributeFilter.summary: One condition on the resource attributes of a record: an attribute key, how to compare it and the value.

key.summary: Attribute key the condition reads. Required.

operator.summary: How the attribute is compared: contains, equals, does not contain, does not equal, exists or does not exist. Defaults to contains.

value.summary: Value the attribute is compared with; empty by default, and not used by the exists operators.

ApmLogScopeAttributeFilter.summary: One condition on the scope attributes of a record: an attribute key, how to compare it and the value.

key.summary: Attribute key the condition reads. Required.

operator.summary: How the attribute is compared: contains, equals, does not contain, does not equal, exists or does not exist. Defaults to contains.

value.summary: Value the attribute is compared with; empty by default, and not used by the exists operators.

ApmLogLogAttributeFilter.summary: One condition on the log attributes of a record: an attribute key, how to compare it and the value.

key.summary: Attribute key the condition reads. Required.

operator.summary: How the attribute is compared: contains, equals, does not contain, does not equal, exists or does not exist. Defaults to contains.

value.summary: Value the attribute is compared with; empty by default, and not used by the exists operators.

ApmSpan.summary: An OpenTelemetry span that Zabbix stores for application performance monitoring, as <c>apmspan.get</c> returns it.

timestamp.summary: Time the span started, as text with nanoseconds (<c>YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.nnnnnnnnn</c>, UTC).

traceid.summary: Trace ID of the span, as hexadecimal text.

spanid.summary: ID of the span, as hexadecimal text.

trace_state.summary: W3C trace state of the span's context, vendor-specific key-value pairs.

span_name.summary: Name of the span, the operation it measures.

span_kind.summary: Kind of the span as OpenTelemetry names it, such as Server, Client, Producer, Consumer or Internal.

service_name.summary: The service that emitted the span, taken from the <c>service.name</c> resource attribute.

resource_attributes.summary: Attributes of the resource that recorded the span, by key.

scope_name.summary: Instrumentation scope that recorded the span, by name.

scope_version.summary: Version of the instrumentation scope that recorded the span.

span_attributes.summary: Attributes of the span, by key.

duration.summary: Duration of the span in nanoseconds.

status_code.summary: Status of the span as OpenTelemetry names it: Unset, Ok or Error.

status_message.summary: Description of the span's status; set mostly for an error.

events.summary: Events recorded during the span, each with its time, name and attributes.

links.summary: Links from the span to spans of other traces, each with the linked trace and span and their attributes.

parent_spanid.summary: ID of the parent span, as hexadecimal text; empty for the root span of a trace.

ApmTrace.summary: An OpenTelemetry trace that Zabbix stores for application performance monitoring, as <c>apmtrace.get</c> returns it: the root span of the trace with the counts of its spans.

timestamp.summary: Time the trace's root span started, as text with nanoseconds (<c>YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.nnnnnnnnn</c>, UTC).

traceid.summary: Trace ID of the span, as hexadecimal text.

spanid.summary: ID of the trace's root span, as hexadecimal text.

trace_state.summary: W3C trace state of the span's context, vendor-specific key-value pairs.

span_name.summary: Name of the span, the operation it measures.

span_kind.summary: Kind of the span as OpenTelemetry names it, such as Server, Client, Producer, Consumer or Internal.

service_name.summary: The service that emitted the span, taken from the <c>service.name</c> resource attribute.

resource_attributes.summary: Attributes of the resource that recorded the span, by key.

scope_name.summary: Instrumentation scope that recorded the span, by name.

scope_version.summary: Version of the instrumentation scope that recorded the span.

span_attributes.summary: Attributes of the span, by key.

duration.summary: Duration of the span in nanoseconds.

status_code.summary: Status of the span as OpenTelemetry names it: Unset, Ok or Error.

status_message.summary: Description of the span's status; set mostly for an error.

events.summary: Events recorded during the span, each with its time, name and attributes.

links.summary: Links from the span to spans of other traces, each with the linked trace and span and their attributes.

error_count.summary: Number of spans in the trace whose status is Error.

ApmSpanEvent.summary: An event recorded during a span.

timestamp.summary: Time the event happened, as text with nanoseconds (UTC).

name.summary: Name of the event.

attributes.summary: Attributes of the event, by key.

ApmTraceEvent.summary: An event recorded during a root span.

timestamp.summary: Time the event happened, as text with nanoseconds (UTC).

name.summary: Name of the event.

attributes.summary: Attributes of the event, by key.

ApmSpanLink.summary: A link from a span to a span of another trace.

traceid.summary: ID of the linked trace, as hexadecimal text.

selects._source: 7.0 selectGroups is the deprecated alias of selectHostGroups (CHost.php, CGraph.php, CTrigger.php 7.0), of selectTemplateGroups on templates (CTemplate.php 7.0); the rest were found by the LIVE drift run over every .get on 7.0.31 and 8.0.0 and read in the service that answers them; map.selectUsers/selectUserGroups/selectLinks/selectLines/selectUrls read the sysmap_user, sysmap_usrgrp, sysmaps_links, sysmap_shape and sysmap_url rows (CMap::addRelatedObjects, 8.0:3724-3830), maintenance.selectTimeperiods the timeperiods rows (CMaintenance::addRelatedObjects), trigger.selectDependencies the triggers a trigger depends on (CTriggerGeneral); host.selectInventory reads the host_inventory row (CHost::addRelatedObjects); sla.selectSchedule answers a list of sla_schedule rows (CSla.php 8.0:352-390), userdirectory.selectProvisionMedia a list of userdirectory_media rows (CUserDirectory.php 8.0:267-290), report.selectUserGroups report_usrgrp rows of usrgrpid and access_userid (CReport.php 8.0:48), and usergroup.selectRights/selectHostGroupRights/selectTemplateGroupRights rights rows of id and permission, the groupid taken out (CUserGroup.php 8.0:1720-1770)

extraFields._source: host.create/update/massadd and hostinterface.* hand interfaces to hostinterface.create (CHost.php:731, CHostInterface.php); the SNMP details are the interface_snmp row; drule.create/update validate dchecks by hand (CDRule::validateDChecks, 7.0:496) and store each as a dchecks row (CDRule::createDChecks), so the list is the dchecks table's columns; map selements carry elements (one id by elementtype) and urls (sysmap_element_url rows), CMapElement.php 8.0:58-170; map.create/update take urls (sysmap_url rows, CMap.php 8.0:2456, 7.0:1748); map.update takes shapes, users and userGroups as map.create validates them, checked on the zbx_array_diff of old and new (CMap.php 8.0:3097-3110), a shape naming its sysmap_shapeid to change it; graph and graph prototype create/update take gitems, the graphs_items rows CGraphGeneral::validateCreate/Update checks by hand (itemid, color required on create; gitemid names an existing one, CGraphGeneral.php 8.0:560-640)

readFields._source: item: CItem::addRelatedObjects reads lastclock/lastns/lastvalue/prevvalue from CHistoryManager::getLastValues; history: the value column is float, integer or text by history table; hostinterface: details is the interface_snmp row (CHostInterface::addRelatedObjects); event.relatedObject is a trigger, discovered host, service or item by the event source (CEvent::addRelatedObjects); template.link_type is what parentTemplates adds (CHostGeneral); module.config is the module manifest object; role.rules is an object of rule lists (CRole::addRelatedObjects); suppression_data is event_suppress rows; apmlog/apmmetric/apmspan/apmtrace answer ClickHouse rows in JSONEachRow (ApmDbClickHouse.php 8.0:155), typed by their columns (CApmData::getClickHouseDbSchema, CApmData.php 8.0:17-170): String and DateTime64(9) as text, Map(String,String) as an object of text, Int64/UInt64 quoted, Float64 and the smaller integers as numbers, Bool as true/false; the nested columns (Events.*, Links.*, Exemplars.*) are lists of objects, one per index (CApmGeneral::translateRowForClickHouse, CApmGeneral.php 8.0:59); an APM metric type is the APM_METRIC_TYPE_* of the table it was read from (CApmMetric.php 8.0:124)

notFields._source: Fields a read (keyed by object) or a request or get (keyed by object.method) does not have although a table or a shared validation names them, each with the source that says so (paths name nested fields: hosts.macros)

template._source: templates share the hosts table (CTemplate.php 8.0:251); template.create/update take none of these, which the IPMI poller, the maintenance manager and low-level discovery keep for hosts (CHost.php 8.0:24 OUTPUT_FIELDS); a template is never IPMI-polled, in maintenance or discovered, so each is its column default

itemprototype._source: the items table's filter columns of a discovery rule (CDiscoveryRule::get moves them into filter, CDiscoveryRule.php 8.0:275); an item prototype has no filter

triggerprototype._source: the triggers table's problem state, which the server keeps for triggers (CTrigger.php 8.0:33 OUTPUT_FIELDS); a prototype is never evaluated, so each is its column default

autoregistration._source: the config column autoregistration.get reads and answers as tls_accept (CAutoregistration.php 7.0:63-64); the reply never carries it under its column name

hostinterface.get._source: a default option of the older get (CHostInterface.php 8.0:51) that no query reads

itemprototype.get._source: accepted by the get rules and never applied to the query (CItemPrototype.php 8.0)

hostinterface.create._source: CHostInterface::checkInput's allow-list (CHostInterface.php 8.0:248) lets the configuration import's own keys through (interface_ref joins an imported interface to its items); createInterfaces stores neither

host.massadd._source: massadd validates the macros at the top level (CHost.php 8.0:884) and hands them to each host internally; CHostBase::validateMacros (CHostBase.php 8.0:1885) then reads them per host, which is not an input

discoveryrule.create._source: the telemetry query fields CItemTypeTelemetryQuery validates (CItemTypeTelemetryQuery.php 8.0:27); a discovery rule's type is one of SUPPORTED_ITEM_TYPES (CDiscoveryRuleGeneral.php 8.0:35), which has no ITEM_TYPE_TELEMETRY_QUERY, and every other type takes each only at its column default (CItemType.php 8.0:58, 517); the extraction dispatches the item type classes without knowing the type

references._source: An id field names the object it refers to by that object's own id field (CApiService::pk(): hostid, templateid, usrgrpid, proxy_groupid, ...); a .get's option of the same name plus s selects by it (item.get hostids). groupid is a host group's except under a template or a template group, whose groups are template groups (CTemplate.php and CTemplateGroup.php validate them against hstgrp type 1). The others name their object by another word: a .get's interfaceids are host interfaces, discoveryids the LLD rule that owns a prototype, druleids/dcheckids/dhostids/dserviceids the network discovery objects, template.get's parentTemplateids templates, event.get's and problem.get's action_userids users, service.get's parentids and childids services

cmdlets._comment: The PowerShell module's reviewed shape where no rule over the description decides it, read by src/Zabbix.Generator (ZabbixCmdletEmitter) from schema/zabbix-api.json. objects.<object>: skip (no generated cmdlet: a hand-written one or a singleton covers it, the value says which), handWrittenGet (the Get- is hand-written), interfaceShorthand (the list field New- also builds one element of from -InterfaceType/-InterfaceIp/-InterfaceDns/-InterfacePort/-UseIp), switches (a two-member enum field taken as a switch: the member sent when present, then when -X:$false), valueForms (the transformation and completion attributes a field's parameter carries), manyPerId (the id field a -Id of that object selects many records by, so -Limit applies with it), names (display and technical: the wire fields of the visible name and of the technical name beside it; a visible name the request calls Name takes -DisplayName, and -Name is an alias of the technical name), unhide (the property a field's parameter takes where its own name would hide a PSCmdlet member, keyed by wire name, its own name kept as an alias; a field not listed takes its name followed by Value). view (the wire fields of the read record's default table, in column order, where the rule over the record does not pick the ones a reader scans for). builders: the New-Zbx<Concept> nested-record builders: the record (its description name), the wire fields taken by position, the help's words (noun, the owner parameters that take it, what it does), valueForms, and ownerSupplied (a required field the owner's command fills when the builder leaves it out, with the sentence the help says). getSwitches: a .get's own flag taken as a switch by every Get- whose parameters carry it. getLists: a .get's own list of enum values taken as an array parameter of that enum by every Get- whose parameters carry it.

builders.use: the -Filter conditions of New-ZbxAction and Set-ZbxAction
builders.what: A condition decides which events an action reacts to: a host group, a trigger severity, a tag value and so on.
An operation is what an action does when its conditions match: send a message, run a script, add a host to a group or link a template.

builders.use: the -Filter conditions of New-ZbxCorrelation and Set-ZbxCorrelation
builders.what: A condition decides which new events an event correlation compares with the problems already open, by tag, tag value or host group.
An operation says what a matching event correlation closes: the old problems, the new event, or both.
A page holds a dashboard's widgets; a dashboard with several pages can cycle through them.
A widget is one tile of a dashboard page, such as a graph, a problem list or a clock, with its position, size and fields.

builders.use: the -Filter conditions of New-ZbxDiscoveryRule and Set-ZbxDiscoveryRule
builders.what: A condition matches a low-level discovery macro against a regular expression, so only the discovered entities that pass become items, triggers and graphs.
A macro path maps a low-level discovery macro to a JSONPath into the discovery data, such as {#FSNAME} to $.fsname.
A step is one request of a web scenario: its URL, what it posts, and the status codes and text it expects back.

ownerSupplied.no: when omitted, New-ZbxHttpTest numbers the step by its position in -Step (1 for the first)

builders.what: A time period says when a maintenance is in effect: once, or every day, week or month at a time of day.
An element is one icon on a network map: a host, a host group, a trigger, another map or a plain image.
A line is a drawn line on a network map, independent of any element.
A link joins two map elements and can change its color while a trigger is in the problem state.
A link trigger draws a map link in its own color and style while its trigger is in the problem state.
A shape is a rectangle or an ellipse drawn on a network map, with optional text.
A problem tag links a service to the problems that carry a matching tag, so they set the service's status.
A status rule raises a service's status when enough of its child services are in a given state.

builders.use: the -Tag of New-ZbxHost, Set-ZbxHost and every other command that tags an object
builders.what: A tag is a name with an optional value, such as env=prod; Zabbix filters problems, actions, permissions and views by tags.
